$comment: Lane 3 API contract catalogue. GET only, read-only, production. Derived from apps/admin-web route->endpoint wiring, backend/internal/permissions/routes.go, contracts/openapi/app-api.yaml, and the tools/perf/hot-paths.*.json inventory. Every requiredField was verified against a real production response.

endpoints.name: admin_web_bootstrap
endpoints.humanFailure: Nobody could open Goat OS at all — the menu and every screen would come up empty, because the server did not describe which pages this person is allowed to see.

endpoints.name: control_tower
endpoints.humanFailure: The home page would show blanks where the counts of things needing attention today should be, so a manager would not know what is urgent.

endpoints.name: action_center
endpoints.humanFailure: The Action Centre list would come up with rows missing their pen name, or showing an internal code instead of a readable status, so nobody could tell what work is outstanding.

endpoints.name: action_center_counts
endpoints.humanFailure: The little count badges at the top of the Action Centre would be blank, so a manager could not see how much work is due against how much is done.

endpoints.name: protocol_adherence
endpoints.humanFailure: The Protocol Adherence page would show a blank percentage instead of how much of the plan was actually done, and rows would not say which pen they refer to.

relations.name: the adherence percentage is its own completed over its own expected
relations.humanFailure: On the vaccination adherence page the percentage is not the completed work divided by the work that was expected, so the headline figure and the counts beside it are two different answers.

relations.name: no more work was completed than was expected
relations.humanFailure: The vaccination adherence page reports more work completed than was ever expected, so the adherence figure is built on a total that does not exist.

endpoints.name: vaccination_command
endpoints.humanFailure: The vaccination command board would show empty boxes where the dose totals should be, so nobody could see how many animals still need their shot.

relations.name: the vaccination board's tiles add up to its own total
relations.humanFailure: On the vaccination board the tiles across the top do not add up to the total above them, so some animals are in the total and in none of the tiles, and nothing on the screen says where they went.

relations.name: no more doses are verified than were due
relations.humanFailure: The vaccination board reports more doses given and checked than there were animals due a dose, so the coverage figure on that board is higher than it can possibly be.

relations.name: no more doses are waiting to be checked than were due
relations.humanFailure: The vaccination board reports more doses waiting to be checked than there were animals due a dose.

endpoints.name: vaccination_command_drives
endpoints.humanFailure: The drive picker on the vaccination board would list blank entries, so a manager could not choose which round of work to look at.

endpoints.name: vaccination_command_cohort_matrix
endpoints.humanFailure: The age-group grid on the vaccination board would be empty, hiding which groups of animals are behind on their shots.

endpoints.name: vaccination_command_shed_dose_matrix
endpoints.page: Vaccination command board (pen and dose grid)
endpoints.humanFailure: The pen-by-dose grid on the vaccination board would be empty, so nobody could see which pens are missing which shot.

endpoints.name: vaccination_execution
endpoints.humanFailure: The vaccination work list would show rows with no pen name and an internal code where the status should be, and the done-versus-target numbers would be blank.

endpoints.name: vaccination_sheds
endpoints.humanFailure: The vaccination pens list would show an internal code instead of a readable status, and the animal counts per pen would be blank.

endpoints.name: vaccination_live_tracker
endpoints.humanFailure: The live tracker would not show who is working today or how far along they are, so nobody could follow the day as it happens.
endpoints.notes: The perf manifests pin a hard-coded business_date that production now rejects; this entry uses today so it cannot go stale.

relations.name: what the drive still owes is what was planned less what actually closed
relations.humanFailure: On the vaccination live tracker the work still outstanding is not the day's plan minus the work that actually finished, so a drive that is still running can show as finished.

relations.name: no more doses closed than were planned for the day
relations.humanFailure: The vaccination live tracker reports more doses finished than were planned for the day.

relations.name: no more doses are waiting to close than were planned for the day
relations.humanFailure: The vaccination live tracker reports more doses waiting to be closed than were planned for the day.

relations.name: the operators listed match the number of operators claimed
relations.humanFailure: The vaccination live tracker says one number of operators are out today and lists a different number, so operators doing the work are missing from the board with nothing to explain it.

relations.name: the pens listed match the number of pens claimed
relations.humanFailure: The vaccination live tracker says one number of pens are being worked today and lists a different number, so pens are missing from the board with nothing to explain it.

relations.name: each operator's outstanding work is their plan less what they closed
relations.humanFailure: On the vaccination live tracker an operator's outstanding work is not their own plan minus the work they finished, so an operator who is done can read as half done and be chased for work they have already completed.

relations.name: an operator appears once on the live tracker
relations.humanFailure: The vaccination live tracker lists the same operator more than once, so their work is counted twice in the day's figures.

relations.name: the pens' planned work adds up to the day's plan
relations.humanFailure: On the vaccination live tracker the pens' own planned figures do not add up to the day's total above them, so part of the day's work belongs to no pen on the board.

relations.name: the operators are not carrying more than the day's plan
relations.humanFailure: The vaccination live tracker lists more operators out today than there are doses planned for the whole day.

endpoints.name: vaccination_drive_assignments
endpoints.humanFailure: The drive assignment list would be empty, so nobody could see which worker is meant to cover which pen.

endpoints.name: vaccination_capacity_config
endpoints.humanFailure: The vaccination settings panel would open blank, so nobody could see or change how many animals a worker is expected to cover in a day.

endpoints.name: vaccination_verification_queue
endpoints.humanFailure: The verification queue would not say how many pieces of proof are waiting to be checked.

endpoints.name: vaccination_schedule
endpoints.humanFailure: The vaccination schedule would be empty, so nobody could see what is planned for the days ahead.

endpoints.name: protocols
endpoints.humanFailure: The vaccination plan page would list unnamed entries, so nobody could tell one plan from another.

endpoints.name: protocol_animal_stages
endpoints.humanFailure: The age-group choices on the vaccination plan would be blank, so nobody could say which animals a rule applies to.

endpoints.name: calendar_events
endpoints.humanFailure: The calendar would show no entries for the week ahead, so nobody could see what work is coming.

endpoints.name: calendar_markers
endpoints.humanFailure: The calendar would lose the dots that show which days have work on them.

endpoints.name: counts_breakdown
endpoints.humanFailure: The counts breakdown would show a blank total where the herd size should be, and the charts would have bars with no numbers behind them.

endpoints.name: counts_herd_analytics
endpoints.humanFailure: The herd analytics page would show blank figures for births, deaths and sales, so the month-on-month picture of the herd would be unreadable.

endpoints.name: counts_mortality
endpoints.humanFailure: The mortality page would show a blank column where the number of deaths by cause should be, hiding whether a problem is getting worse.
endpoints.notes: Not covered by any hot-paths manifest before this lane.

endpoints.name: counts_milk_preparation
endpoints.humanFailure: The milk preparation list would be empty, so the team would not know how much to mix for the kids today.

endpoints.name: herd_register_summary
endpoints.humanFailure: The herd register would show blanks instead of how many animals are alive, sold or dead.
endpoints.notes: Grouping keys such as park and breed are legitimately empty on the rollup row, so only the counts are asserted.

endpoints.name: goat_search
endpoints.humanFailure: Searching for an animal would return nothing, so a worker could not pull up an animal's record.

endpoints.name: weighing_shed_weights
endpoints.humanFailure: The weights page would show a blank column where the average daily gain should be, so nobody could tell whether the animals are growing.
endpoints.notes: Uses a rolling 30-day window; the perf manifests pin fixed dates that age out.

relations.name: every weighed animal is in one of the two ways of weighing
relations.humanFailure: On the Weights page the animals weighed one at a time and the animals weighed as a whole pen do not add up to the number of animals the page says were weighed. Some pens are being left out of the totals, so every average and every gain figure on that page speaks for fewer animals than it claims.

relations.name: the Weights headline average is its own total over its own head count
relations.humanFailure: On the Weights page the average weight is not the total weight divided by the number of animals weighed. The headline average is not the average of what was actually put on the scale.

relations.name: each pen's average on the Weights page is its own total over its own head count
relations.humanFailure: On the Weights page a pen's average weight is not that pen's total divided by the animals in it, so the pen's row and the figure beside it are two different answers.

relations.name: a pen appears once on the Weights page
relations.humanFailure: The Weights page lists the same pen of the same farm more than once, so that pen's animals are counted twice in every total on the page and its history is split between the two rows.

relations.name: no more pens were weighed than exist
relations.humanFailure: The Weights page says more pens were weighed than there are pens in the selected farm and period.

relations.name: the heavier sale band sits inside the lighter one
relations.humanFailure: On the Weights page more animals are reported at the heavier sale weight than at the lighter one, which cannot be true, so the sale-ready counts on that page are wrong.

relations.name: the sale-ready count sits inside the animals it was measured from
relations.humanFailure: On the Weights page more animals are reported as ready to sell than were weighed to decide it.

endpoints.name: weighing_weight_demographics
endpoints.humanFailure: The weight analytics charts would come up empty, hiding how the herd is spread across weight bands.

endpoints.name: weighing_leadership_growth
endpoints.humanFailure: The growth page would lose its headline gain figure and the pen leaderboard, so nobody could see which pens are falling behind.

relations.name: the losing-animals tile and the list it opens agree
relations.humanFailure: On the Growth page the tile counting the animals that are losing weight does not match the list of animals it opens, so one of the two is wrong and there is no way to tell which.

relations.name: an animal's daily gain is the weight it gained over the days it took
relations.humanFailure: On the Growth page an animal's daily gain is not the weight it actually gained divided by the days between its two weighings, so the gain figures on that page are not the movement they are built on.

relations.name: the animals losing weight sit inside the animals the gain figure speaks for
relations.humanFailure: On the Growth page more animals are reported as losing weight than the daily gain figure above them counts at all.

relations.name: the farms add up to the herd on the Growth page
relations.humanFailure: On the Growth page the per-farm animal counts do not add up to the herd figure above them, so some animals belong to no farm on that page and the herd daily gain speaks for a different group than the cards beneath it.

relations.name: a pen appears once on the Growth leaderboard
relations.humanFailure: The Growth page lists the same pen of the same farm twice on its leaderboard, so that pen's history is split in two and neither row tells the whole story for it.

relations.name: the animals with two weighings sit inside the animals weighed
relations.humanFailure: On the Growth page more animals are reported as weighed twice than were weighed at all.

relations.name: a farm that weighed animals has gain figures to show for it
relations.humanFailure: The Growth page counts animals as weighed in this period and then shows no weekly gain at all for them, so a page with real weighings on it reads as though nothing was measured.

endpoints.name: growth_director_weights
endpoints.humanFailure: The growth director view would show blanks where the counts of animals ready for sale should be.

endpoints.name: feed_analytics_execution
endpoints.humanFailure: The feed analytics page would show an empty day-by-day chart, so nobody could see whether feed actually went out.

endpoints.name: feed_analytics_stock
endpoints.humanFailure: The feed stock view would not say how much feed is left or how many days it will last, so the farm could run out without warning.

endpoints.name: feed_analytics_directed
endpoints.humanFailure: The directed feed view would be empty, hiding what each pen was actually told to eat.

endpoints.name: feed_direction_preview
endpoints.humanFailure: The feed direction screen would not show today's plan, so the team would not know what to feed which pen.
endpoints.notes: The perf manifests send a parameter production no longer accepts, so they record a request failure rather than a real check.

endpoints.name: feed_packing_worklist
endpoints.humanFailure: The feed packing list would be empty, so the team would not know what to weigh out and bag this morning.

endpoints.name: feed_config_feed_items
endpoints.humanFailure: The feed settings page would list unnamed feed items, so nobody could build or edit a ration.

endpoints.name: sales_overview
endpoints.humanFailure: The sales page would show a blank where the revenue figure should be, and the month-by-month bars would have no numbers behind them.

endpoints.name: sales_deals
endpoints.humanFailure: The list of sales deals would be empty, so nobody could check what was sold and to whom.

endpoints.name: procurement_vendors
endpoints.humanFailure: The vendor list would show unnamed suppliers, so nobody could tell who an animal or a feed load came from.

endpoints.name: procurement_source_entry_loads
endpoints.humanFailure: The arriving-loads list would be empty, so nobody could check in a new batch of animals.

endpoints.name: verification_queue
endpoints.humanFailure: The verify queue would show rows with no worker name and nothing to identify what is being checked, so a verifier could not do their round.

endpoints.name: verification_oversight_analytics
endpoints.humanFailure: The verify oversight charts would be empty, hiding how big the backlog of unchecked work has grown.

endpoints.name: toxin_review
endpoints.humanFailure: The toxin review list would be empty, so a suspected feed poisoning case could sit unreviewed.

endpoints.name: work_board_page
endpoints.humanFailure: The work board would not list today's jobs, so nobody could see what the team is meant to be doing.
endpoints.notes: Park id is the one the perf manifests already pin; it is read-only and stable.

endpoints.name: admin_workforce_people
endpoints.humanFailure: The people page would list unnamed staff, so nobody could assign work to a person.

endpoints.name: admin_roster_coverage
endpoints.humanFailure: The cover page would not show who is standing in for whom, so a pen could be left unattended.

endpoints.name: admin_locations
endpoints.humanFailure: Pens and farms would appear unnamed across the whole system, so no screen could say where anything is.

endpoints.name: admin_sops
endpoints.humanFailure: The standard procedures list would be empty, so workers would have no steps to follow and no proof to capture.

endpoints.name: health_analytics
endpoints.humanFailure: The health analytics page would show empty charts, hiding which illnesses are spreading.
endpoints.notes: Not covered by any hot-paths manifest before this lane.

endpoints.name: health_config_protocols
endpoints.humanFailure: The health settings page would list no treatment rules, so nobody could say how a sick animal should be treated.

endpoints.name: operations_kernel_health
endpoints.humanFailure: The operations health panel would not say whether the system is keeping up with its own background work, so a silent backlog could build unnoticed.

endpoints.name: operations_outbox_delivery
endpoints.humanFailure: Messages the system passes between its own parts are stuck, so something a worker recorded on the phone could quietly never reach the dashboard at all.
endpoints.notes: Picked up from lane 2, which parked messages-not-stuck-in-the-outbox as infrastructure health belonging to lane 3. The verdict is the backend own status field, not a threshold invented here.

endpoints.name: operations_audit_summary
endpoints.humanFailure: The operations audit summary would not load, so nobody could see a roll-up of what changed recently.

endpoints.name: herd_signals_live
endpoints.humanFailure: The herd signals page would show no live readings, so a collar or gateway could go dark without anyone noticing.

endpoints.name: alerts_config
endpoints.humanFailure: The alerts page would not say which alerts are switched on, so an important warning could be off without anyone knowing.

endpoints.name: leadership_tasks
endpoints.humanFailure: The tasks board would show cards with no title, so nobody could tell what a piece of work is.

endpoints.name: leadership_tasks_assignees
endpoints.humanFailure: The tasks board could not offer anyone to assign work to.

endpoints.name: admin_web_counts_approvals
endpoints.humanFailure: The approvals page would not list what is waiting on a manager's decision, so a death report or a correction could sit forever.
endpoints.notes: Registered and probed by the perf manifests but absent from the OpenAPI contract, so only presence of the list is asserted.

endpoints.name: operations_dlq_list
endpoints.humanFailure: The DLQ Center would not list the work that got stuck on its way from the phone to the dashboard, which is the only place that work ever appears.
endpoints.notes: Added 2026-09-23: the kernel-health entry reads a status summary; nothing read the list the page itself renders.

endpoints.name: ceo_ai_starters
endpoints.humanFailure: The Ask Mesha panel would not offer its opening questions, and because the dashboard decides whether to show the panel at all from this same answer, the assistant would disappear from the screen entirely.
endpoints.notes: Added 2026-09-23: the assistant had no endpoint in this catalogue at all. Its answer endpoint is a POST, which this read-only lane may never call, so the launcher probe is the part that can be watched.
